<thought>From the 13C NMR data, the low‑field aliphatic carbon signals (≈ 26–44 ppm) correspond to carbons in methyl or methylene groups. The peaks at 26.90 ppm (appearing twice) and 26.18 ppm are typical for CH₃ carbons. The signal at 44.06 ppm is more down‑field, usually indicating a carbon attached to an electronegative atom (e.g., O‑CH₃) and also represents a methyl carbon. Thus there are three distinct methyl carbon signals, meaning the molecule contains three CH₃ groups. If any of the 34.54 ppm signals were methyl, they would appear slightly up‑field, but they are more consistent with CH₂ carbons. Therefore the number of CH₃ groups is 3.</thought>
<final_answer>3</final_answer>
